literal: Strangers to be satisfied, one's own people will starve, when a fool great wealth acquires.
translation: When a fool acquires great wealth, strangers will feast to their heart's content while his own relatives starve.
modern: ஒரு அறிவிலி பெரும் செல்வத்தை அடையும் போது, அவனுடைய உறவினர்கள் பசியால் வாட, அந்நியர்கள் அந்தச் செல்வத்தை முழுமையாக அனுபவிப்பார்கள்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the tragic misdirection of resources when a fool gains wealth. The word 'தமர்' refers to one's own family and relatives, who naturally deserve support, while 'ஏதிலார்' refers to strangers or outsiders. Instead of helping those close to him, the fool squanders his fortune on outsiders who flatter him, leaving his own kin to starve ('பசிப்பர்'). The term 'கடை' is used here in a temporal sense to mean 'when' or 'at the time of' acquiring wealth.
